overview: Andorra is a tiny country high in the Pyrenees, between France and Spain. Its capital, Andorra la Vella, is the highest capital city in Europe. Andorra is a co-principality: its two heads of state are the Bishop of Urgell in Spain and the President of France. Catalan is the official language, and tourism, especially skiing and shopping, is the main source of income.

geography.text: Andorra is landlocked and almost entirely mountainous, made up of deep valleys surrounded by peaks of the Pyrenees. The Valira river and its branches run through the country, and almost all of its towns sit in the valley floors. Snowy winters make it a popular place for skiing.

history.text: Andorra's independence is traditionally traced back to the time of Charlemagne. Since 1278 it has been ruled jointly by two co-princes, today the Bishop of Urgell in Spain and the President of France. Andorra stayed out of Europe's wars, and in 1993 it adopted its first written constitution and became a parliamentary democracy.

events.title: Joint rule agreed
events.text: An agreement between the Count of Foix and the Bishop of Urgell sets up rule by two co-princes.

events.title: Council of the Land
events.text: Andorra's assembly is founded, one of the oldest parliaments in Europe.

events.title: First constitution
events.text: Andorra becomes a parliamentary democracy and joins the United Nations.

government.text: Andorra has two heads of state, called co-princes: the Bishop of Urgell in Spain and the President of France. Their role is mostly ceremonial. Andorrans elect a parliament, the General Council, which chooses the head of government.

economy.text: Andorra's economy is built on tourism. Millions of visitors come each year to ski in winter, hike in summer and shop, because goods have long been cheaper there than in Spain and France. Banking is also important. Andorra uses the euro, although it is not in the European Union.

culture.text: Catalan is Andorra's only official language, and Andorra is the only country where that is the case. Small stone Romanesque churches dot its valleys. Most people living in Andorra are not Andorran citizens but residents from Spain, Portugal and France.

items.title: Romanesque churches
items.text: Small stone churches built from the 1000s to the 1200s, such as Sant Joan de Caselles.

items.title: Catalan
items.text: The only country in the world where Catalan is the sole official language.

sport.text: Skiing is Andorra's best-known sport, and its resorts host World Cup races. The national football team, made up mostly of part-time players, has won only a handful of competitive matches.

items.title: Grandvalira
items.text: One of the largest ski areas in the Pyrenees, a regular World Cup venue.
Andorra beat North Macedonia 1–0, its first ever competitive win.
